We need to write formative feedback as JSON. Address student as "you". Be specific, supportive, actionable. Cite sections/figures. Name what they did well, state what next rubric level requires. Don't change marks. Don't comment on conversion artefacts. Don't make up explanations for unclear/incomplete reasoning from marking agent.

Schema: summary <=80 words, next_steps array of 3 strings, criteria object mapping criterion id to feedback <=70 words each.

We need craft feedback for C1-C4. Include summary and next steps. Ensure no markdown, no prose outside JSON.

Let's draft.

Summary: "Your report has a clear mission rationale and a readable, well-structured presentation. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, you need formal, quantitative mission requirements and real preliminary technical results, plus a more robust plan with contingencies and dependencies. Your presentation is already strong; tighten the reference list so every source is cited and matched."

<=80 words. Count roughly 60.

Next steps: 3 strings. Actionable:
1. "Add a formal requirements table in Mission Concept & Rationale covering coverage, revisit, resolution, spectral bands, data latency, lifetime and payload, each tied to user needs and cited where appropriate."
2. "In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, include at least one quantitative preliminary result (e.g. STK orbit/coverage output, launch or link-budget calculation, power/thermal sizing) with brief interpretation, and add contingencies, task dependencies and resource estimates to the Gantt."
3. "Revise the end-of-life plan to justify deorbit or a graveyard orbit for LEO, and clean up Useful Links so every listed source is cited in text and matches the reference list."

Criteria feedback <=70 words each.

C1: "You clearly explain why the Great Barrier Reef needs dedicated monitoring and identify users such as marine and conservation scientists. To reach Accomplished, add formal mission objectives and quantitative requirements—coverage, revisit, resolution, spectral bands, data latency, lifetime and payload—and link each to user needs with appropriate references. Also correct the ocean acidification wording to a ~30% increase in H+ concentration / ~0.1 pH decrease." Count ~70? Let's count: You(1) clearly2 explain3 why4 the5 Great6 Barrier7 Reef8 needs9 dedicated10 monitoring11 and12 identify13 users14 such15 as16 marine17 and18 conservation19 scientists20. To21 reach22 Accomplished23, add24 formal25 mission26 objectives27 and28 quantitative29 requirements30—coverage31, revisit32, resolution33, spectral34 bands35, data36 latency37, lifetime38 and39 payload40—and41 link42 each43 to44 user45 needs46 with47 appropriate48 references49. Also50 correct51 the52 ocean53 acidification54 wording55 to56 a57 ~30%58 increase59 in60 H+61 concentration62 /63 ~0.1 pH64 decrease65. Good ~65.

C2: "Your Gantt chart and task descriptions make the plan believable and connect to orbit selection and STK work. To reach Accomplished, add contingencies, task dependencies and resource estimates, and explain why the plan is structured this way for this mission. Integrate information sources into the plan rather than listing them separately, and cite them where used." Count ~60.

C3: "You report background reading and completion of STK tutorials 1–4, which shows useful preparation. To reach Accomplished, include actual preliminary technical results—for example STK orbit/coverage outputs, launch or link-budget calculations, power/thermal sizing, or COE/AOE values—with a brief description and interpretation. This will provide the evidence that you are on track for completion." ~60.

C4: "Your headings, readable prose, consistent formatting and labelled Gantt chart make the report easy to follow. To secure the top level, add a formal caption to Image 1 and ensure every source in Useful Links is cited in the text and matches the reference list; remove duplicates and uncited links. Your presentation is already strong." ~60.
